overview: Perseus Mining is an ASX/TSX-listed, Africa-focused gold producer operating three mines: Edikan in Ghana, and Sissingué and Yaouré (including the CMA Underground) in Côte d'Ivoire. The company is developing its fourth mine, the Nyanzaga Gold Project in Tanzania, targeting first gold in January 2027, and produced 404,998 ounces of gold in FY2026 at an all-in site cost of US$1,750/oz. Perseus generates cash almost entirely from gold sales, funding a growing dividend and on-market share buyback while pursuing organic growth and selective M&A across West and East Africa.

business_model.summary: Perseus is a single-commodity gold miner that extracts, processes and sells gold doré/bullion into the international spot market at prevailing prices; it has no long-term offtake contracts of significance, so realized price essentially tracks the spot gold price. Revenue is transactional (tonnes milled × grade × recovery × gold price) rather than recurring, and is highly leveraged to gold price and production volumes across four assets in three countries.

revenue_streams.name: Edikan (Ghana)
revenue_streams.trend: stable/mine-life extension via Fetish and Esuajah North cutbacks

revenue_streams.name: Yaouré open pit (Côte d'Ivoire)
revenue_streams.trend: declining as ore shifts to CMA Underground

revenue_streams.name: CMA Underground (Yaouré, Côte d'Ivoire)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, first gold FY26, commercial production targeted Q3 FY27

revenue_streams.name: Nyanzaga (Tanzania, development)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, first gold targeted January 2027, will become 4th mine

business_model.customer_type: B2B/commodity market — gold sold to bullion banks/refiners at prevailing spot/realized prices; no reliance on individual customer relationships
business_model.geographic_mix: Ghana ~39%, Côte d'Ivoire ~61% of FY26 production (Yaouré + CMA + Sissingué); Tanzania (Nyanzaga) in development, first production expected FY27; corporate offices in Perth, Dubai, Abidjan, Accra and Dar es Salaam

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier, multi-mine, multi-jurisdictional African gold producer (~400-480koz/yr); smaller than sector leader Endeavour Mining (largest pure-play West African producer, ~US$6.7-13.6bn market cap) but larger than Resolute Mining (~AU$2.0bn); Perseus market cap ~AU$6.5bn as of mid-2026

moat_factors.description: Operations spread across Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and (soon) Tanzania reduce single-country political/regulatory risk relative to single-asset peers
7.0Moz Proved & Probable reserves and 10.6Moz Measured & Indicated resources; Nyanzaga mine life extended to 16 years in FY26
US$1.03bn cash and bullion, US$400m syndicated debt facility upsized in FY26 giving >US$1.4bn total liquidity, positioning Perseus as a capital-flexible consolidator
Long operating history and negotiated agreements with Ghanaian, Ivorian and Tanzanian governments, plus free-carried interests that align government economics
Recognized mid-tier operator but lacks the scale, cost leadership or trading liquidity of Endeavour Mining or major diversified miners

weaknesses: No pricing power — pure price-taker on a globally traded commodity
Concentration in politically higher-risk West/East African jurisdictions (coup risk, resource nationalism, royalty increases)
Aging Edikan and open-pit Yaouré ore bodies require continual cutback capital to sustain grade and output
Recently failed in a major consolidation attempt (Predictive Discovery), suggesting execution/competitive limits in contested M&A processes
Nyanzaga is a single large capital project with execution and ramp-up risk concentrated in one new jurisdiction (Tanzania)

growth_drivers: Nyanzaga Gold Project (Tanzania) — fourth mine, first gold targeted January 2027, reserve base expanded 73% to 4.1Moz in FY26, mine life extended to 16 years
CMA Underground at Yaouré — Côte d'Ivoire's first mechanised underground mine, ramping toward commercial production in Q3 FY27, extending Yaouré's economic life
Exploration pipeline — active drilling at Yaouré, Ghana priority targets, and reconnaissance permits secured in Guinea (5 of 7 applications approved)
Edikan life extension — Fetish and Esuajah North pit cutbacks expected to add ~300,000 ounces to mine life
Five-year production outlook of 515,000-535,000 oz/year at average AISC of US$1,400-1,500/oz once Nyanzaga ramps up, versus FY26's 405koz

Selective M&A/consolidation optionality — 9.9% strategic stake in Aurum Resources (Côte d'Ivoire explorer, ~4.4Moz across Boundiali/Napié, adjacent to Sissingué/Bagoé); upsized US$400m debt facility supports further bolt-on or larger deals
Capital returns — increasing dividend (final dividend raised to 9.0 A-cents/share, up from 5.0 cps) and expanded A$150m on-market buyback signal confidence and provide a re-rating catalyst

business.description: Yaouré open pit and Edikan both saw materially lower head grades and higher costs in FY26 as easier ore is mined out, requiring continual reserve replacement
100% revenue derived from gold sales with no diversification into other metals or revenue streams
US$523m project is 67% complete; delays or cost overruns before January 2027 first gold would materially affect the growth thesis
Perseus's A$2.1bn bid for Predictive Discovery was outbid by a matched Robex Resources offer in Dec 2025, highlighting competitive intensity in West African gold consolidation

financial.description: Costs incurred in local African currencies and US dollars while gold is sold in USD; local currency depreciation/inflation and rising royalty regimes increased AISC in FY26

financial.risk: Rising debt utilization for growth capex
financial.description: US$400m syndicated facility upsized in FY26 to fund Nyanzaga and CMA Underground; while currently well covered by cash flow, increased leverage raises risk if gold prices fall
Balancing large buyback (A$150m), rising dividends, and ~US$530m FY27 growth capex requires sustained strong cash generation

regulatory.description: Higher royalty regimes in both Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana directly increased AISC in FY26; African governments have shown willingness to increase mining taxes/royalties as gold prices rise

Operations and development concentrated in Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and Tanzania — jurisdictions exposed to coups, resource nationalism, and shifting mining codes (West Africa has seen multiple recent regional coups)
10-20% free-carried government stakes in each mine dilute Perseus's economic interest and could expand under renegotiated mining codes

macro.description: Revenue and profitability are directly and almost entirely a function of the spot gold price; FY26 profit surge was driven primarily by average realized price rising from US$2,543 to US$3,693/oz, not volume growth
Regional security and terrorism risk (e.g., Sahel instability) requires ongoing investment in personnel security and evacuation planning
Falling real interest rates have been a tailwind for gold prices; a reversal (rising real rates) is a key macro risk to the gold price underpinning current earnings

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold prices remained elevated and supportive through FY26 (average realized price of US$3,693/oz, up from US$2,543/oz in FY25), driven by central bank buying, geopolitical uncertainty and real-rate dynamics, though prices softened somewhat in H2 FY26. West African gold miners are in an active consolidation phase (Perseus-Predictive-Robex contest, other regional M&A) as majors and mid-tiers seek reserve growth amid depleting existing mines.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — earnings are highly cyclical and geared to the gold price cycle; production volumes are comparatively stable but AISC and margins swing significantly with grade, strip ratio and royalty changes
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect but significant — gold (a non-yielding asset) tends to benefit from falling real interest rates and a weaker US dollar; rate hikes or a stronger USD are historically headwinds for gold prices and therefore Perseus's revenue
key_input_costs: Royalties (rising in Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire)

recent_developments.event: FY2026 annual results released: record profit after tax of US$480.5m (up 13.9%), revenue of US$1.48bn (up 18.9%), record notional operating cashflow of US$769m, NTA per share up 28% to US$1.79; final dividend raised to 9.0 A-cents/share
On-market share buyback expanded from initial A$100m to A$150m; A$126.7m deployed in FY26 (cumulative ~A$183.5m since Aug-2024 at average A$4.07/share); stock hit all-time highs in September 2026
Completed divestment of 70% interest in Meyas Sand Gold Project (Sudan) for US$260m cash, sharpening strategic focus on core West/East African assets
Acquired a 9.9% strategic stake in Aurum Resources (ASX:AUE) for A$23.69m, gaining exposure to ~3-4.4Moz resource adjacent to the Sissingué/Bagoé operation
Withdrew its unsolicited A$2.1bn (US$1.38bn) all-scrip takeover bid for Predictive Discovery after rival Robex Resources matched the offer; Predictive/Robex proceeded with their merger instead
Upsized syndicated debt facility to US$400m, providing total cash and undrawn debt capacity of >US$1.4bn to fund growth and support further M&A optionality
Craig Jones assumed role of Managing Director and CEO (effective 1 Oct 2025), succeeding long-serving Jeff Quartermaine who retired after leading Perseus for over a decade
Wade Bickley appointed Chief Operating Officer; Thomas (Tommy) McKeith joined the Board as Non-Executive Director post year-end

CMA Underground (Yaouré) achieved first gold and commenced stoping operations (April 2026), on track for commercial production in Q3 FY27; Nyanzaga reached 67% construction progress against the US$523m budget, on schedule for first gold January 2027

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Report / Q4 FY26 results (August 2026)

items.notes: Confirmed unchanged from earlier guidance; includes initial contribution from Nyanzaga in H2 FY27
Higher than FY26 actual of US$1,750/oz; reflects transitional year costs from Nyanzaga ramp-up, CMA Underground development and Edikan/Yaouré strip-ratio and mine-plan transitions
Includes ~US$230m for Nyanzaga completion, ~US$80m for CMA Underground development at Yaouré, and ~US$140m for strategic cutbacks at Edikan
Reflects full ramp-up of Nyanzaga and CMA Underground contributing alongside existing operations
Costs expected to normalize lower than the FY27 transitional guidance range as Nyanzaga reaches steady-state production

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Craig Jones (first full year at helm since 1 Oct 2025) emphasized safe execution, operational discipline and disciplined capital allocation balancing growth investment with shareholder returns. Management highlighted the upsized US$400m debt facility and record cash/bullion position (US$1.03bn) as giving Perseus flexibility to pursue further growth opportunities while continuing the on-market buyback and dividend. Gold prices were noted as supportive through FY26 but softening in H2, and management does not appear to hedge materially, remaining fully leveraged to spot gold prices.

bull_case: Record FY26 profit (US$480m, +13.9%) and cashflow (US$769m notional operating cashflow) driven by strong realized gold prices (US$3,693/oz), with a growing dividend (final dividend up 80% to 9.0 A-cents) and expanded A$150m buyback returning capital to shareholders
Clear, funded production growth pipeline — CMA Underground (Q3 FY27) and Nyanzaga (Jan 2027) both nearing production, underpinning a five-year outlook of 515-535koz/yr, up from FY26's 405koz

Fortress balance sheet with US$1.03bn cash/bullion and >US$1.4bn total liquidity after debt facility upsize to US$400m, providing resilience and optionality for further bolt-on M&A (e.g., Aurum Resources stake) without straining the balance sheet
Jurisdictional and asset diversification across Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and (soon) Tanzania reduces reliance on any single mine or country relative to single-asset peers
Full leverage to a supportive gold price environment (record prices through FY26) with no material hedging, so shareholders capture the full upside if gold prices remain elevated or rise further
bear_case: FY26 earnings growth was driven almost entirely by a higher realized gold price (+45% YoY), not volume or cost improvement — Yaouré and Edikan volumes and grades declined, and Group AISC rose to the top of guidance (US$1,750/oz); a gold price correction would expose underlying cost pressure

FY27 guidance shows AISC rising further to US$1,835-2,070/oz, a transitional-year cost blowout as Nyanzaga ramps and strip ratios/royalties increase at existing mines, meaning near-term margins likely compress even if production grows

Elevated jurisdictional/political risk concentrated in West and East Africa (Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Tanzania), including rising royalty regimes already evident in FY26 and broader regional coup/instability risk affecting the wider Sahel/West Africa region

Nyanzaga is a large, single-project bet in a new jurisdiction (Tanzania) for Perseus; delays or cost overruns on the US$523m project (67% complete at FY26 year-end) would directly undermine the medium-term growth and cost-reduction thesis

Failed, costly pursuit of Predictive Discovery (A$2.1bn bid withdrawn after being outbid) illustrates execution risk and competitive intensity in West African gold consolidation, and raises questions about capital discipline in future M&A attempts
